title: ALMA Observations of Giant Molecular Clouds in the Starburst Dwarf Galaxy Henize 2-10
question: What are the molecular gas distribution and giant molecular cloud properties in the starburst dwarf Henize 2-10, and how do they compare with Milky Way and other galaxies?

evidence.quote: at a distance of $8.7$ Mpc (cite: Tully_1988)
We take their resulting measurement of $12+\log(\rm{O/H})=8.55\pm0.02$ $(\sim 0.7\ensuremath{Z_\odot})$ to be the most reliable in the literature

what.value: Comparison GMC catalogs for Milky Way, LMC, NGC 300, IC 10, II Zw 40

evidence.quote: we compare their scaling relations to those of clouds in a sample of galaxies collected from the literature.

external_data.citation: (cite: Heyer_2009; Oka_2001; Wong_2011; Faesi_2018; Leroy_2006; Kepley_2016)

recipe.method: Manual CASA calibration, continuum subtraction in uv, multiscale CLEAN with natural weighting, primary beam correction
Sum integrated-intensity map to get mass with Galactic XCO; Gaussian fit to spectrum; plane fit to moment 1; PV diagram and dynamical mass
key_parameters: masked cube: seed pairs of channels >5 sigma, expand to >1.5 sigma
assumptions: XCO = 2e20 cm^-2 (K km/s)^-1, factor 1.36 for helium, distance 8.7 Mpc, edge-on rotation for dynamical mass

recipe.method: CPROPS with default parameters, modified CLUMPFIND, extrapolation to 0 K, beam and channel deconvolution
key_parameters: 4 sigma seed, 2 sigma edge, 15 pc x 15 pc x 2 km/s moving box
assumptions: alpha_CO = 4.35 Msun (K km/s pc^2)^-1; Mvir=1040 R sigma_v^2 (spherical, rho~R^-1)

recipe.method: Truncated power-law maximum-likelihood fit of cumulative mass distribution above completeness limit
Pearson correlations, orthogonal distance regression for size-linewidth, bilinear least squares for Mvir-Mlum and Mlum-R; virial alphaCO
assumptions: Single Milky Way alpha_CO for all clouds

evidence.quote: yields a molecular gas mass of $(1.2\pm 0.4)\times 10^8~\ensuremath{M_\odot}$
a total integrated CO intensity of $I_{\rm CO}=146\pm 3$ K km s$^{-1}$
we identify 178 clouds, of which 59 are unresolved
the median value is $3.7$ $M_\odot$ (K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$)$^{-1}$
The median surface density is $180$ $M_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$

not_stated_but_needed: Multiscale CLEAN scales, threshold and gain

rediscovery_reason: Data public, CPROPS recipe with defaults and numeric results (cloud counts, slopes) are checkable.
